blocks.text: ADR: React admin for stock, WordPress stays the public storefront

This is the working cut for LSH-ADR-2024-029 on April 2, 2024. Luis Ortega asked for a written bound after the current path (Woo public, React admin in staging) stopped being honest. I am Michael Gilfilian, Web Developer, writing for Luis Ortega, Cole Brennan, and Mara Singh. Primary host admin.lakeshore.internal. If you are skimming, jump the decision callout, then the refuse on React storefront for four public sites, then open questions. If you are implementing next week, jump the constraints, the numbers table, and the commands or contracts.

Public site stays Woo. Stock admin is React. This ADR exists so a contractor cannot reopen the storefront rewrite without Luis. I am not restating a hallway yes. React storefront for four public sites is out because SEO, pickup plugin, and Mara's reporting all sit on Woo. A rewrite is a second company. Cost of doing nothing is already in the numbers: look at sites=4, admin=1, weeks=0, seo=12.4, plugins=22, rewrite=28.5, stores=4, adr=1. Sibling tickets LSH-5280 and LSH-TDD-2023-058. I will not reopen React storefront for four public sites in a side thread because a vendor sent a discount. Cole Brennan is the acceptor unless the owners line says otherwise.
Decision for leadership

blocks.label: Decision
blocks.text: Public site stays Woo. Stock admin is React. This ADR exists so a contractor cannot reopen the storefront rewrite without Luis.

Background on admin.lakeshore.internal. Woo public, React admin in staging. That is the system Luis Ortega lives with, not a slide. I timed or pulled the leftover on woo-prod.lakeshore.internal the week before this file. Lag, stale minutes, or miss counts in this file are from that pull, not a round number I liked. Ticket LSH-ADR-2024-029 names the pull. If those numbers moved after April 2, 2024, update this file in review, do not 'correct' them in Slack.

blocks.text: Background. Why the current path is the wrong tool

Mara Singh owns a leftover that is easy to skip: inv-api.lakeshore.internal. I will ping once. After that the owner is late, not blocked. Unique to this file (38): refuse on React storefront for four public sites, lock is split UI, Woo public, React admin, Luis is acceptor. I will not hide a product change inside a 'quick align' on LSH-5280.
Do not rebuild the four public sites in React to make the admin prettier.

What a skeptical user would try first on admin.lakeshore.internal: the path Luis Ortega actually has, not a desktop demo. Metric I will argue is time-to-useful, not a vanity QPS. If we cannot show that path on woo-prod.lakeshore.internal with the numbers already in this file, we do not have a cut. Michael Gilfilian will not accept a laptop screenshot as that proof.
Constraints and the lock

blocks.label: Lock
blocks.text: split UI, Woo public, React admin, Luis is acceptor Host admin.lakeshore.internal. Ticket LSH-5280. Acceptor Luis Ortega.

Open clock: split UI, Woo public, React admin, Luis is acceptor. If that clock collides with a freeze, the date moves and the scope does not. Luis Ortega hears the new date on LSH-ADR-2024-029. I will not book a change in the last 40 minutes of a freeze because it is 'just config.' Config is a change. Host if we have to prove a count: admin.lakeshore.internal.

I will not mix clocks to make admin.lakeshore.internal look healthier.

Named leftover unique to LSH-ADR-2024-029

woo-prod.lakeshore.internal is in this file because skipping it is how the last near-miss happened. Mara Singh owns the check. I want a count on LSH-TDD-2023-058 before anyone says the leftover is 'implied.' Implied leftovers are how React storefront for four public sites almost returned.
What I will not claim in LSH-ADR-2024-029

I will not claim React storefront for four public sites is impossible for a competitor. I will claim we will not buy it. I will not claim zero incidents after this cut. I will claim the next one dies at the gate named in the lock. Host admin.lakeshore.internal.
First useful slice for LSH-5280

First useful is split UI, Woo public, React admin, Luis is acceptor, not a prettier theme or a bigger box. Luis Ortega sees that slice on admin.lakeshore.internal. If the slice needs a second product, that is a new ticket and Luis Ortega is in the thread. I will not hide it inside LSH-ADR-2024-029.
